paper.title_en: Matrix valued Hawking transport and channel covariance for magnetically supported generalized Hayward black holes
paper.abstract_en: We formulate semiclassical Hawking transport for a one parameter set of generalized Hayward geometries supported by member specific magnetic nonlinear electrodynamic completions, using the established gauge invariant two channel gravitational and electromagnetic perturbation system and its flux normalized transmission matrices. The matrix greybody description retains channel conversion and parity dependence and generates the outgoing occupation covariance without replacing the coupled system by auxiliary scalar channels. In the coupled quadrupolar sector, the luminosity falls by more than two orders of magnitude between <math altimg="si77.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1830"><mi>χ</mi></math> = 0.2 and 0.9, whereas the electromagnetic share rises from 15.5% to 19.8%. The thermally integrated flux is almost entirely carried by the bright greybody eigenchannel. Rotation to the asymptotic gravitational and electromagnetic basis produces a nonzero, basis specified mutual information flux of about 3% of the marginal entropy in the strong core regime; the outgoing gravitational/electromagnetic state remains separable, so this correlation is not an entanglement or information recovery diagnostic. The coarse grained entropy excess over reversible Clausius transfer is nonnegative frequency by frequency and channel by channel. An effective Reissner–Nordström comparison shows that the strong core change in luminosity is dominated by the temperature difference and that most of the channel mutual information is already present in ordinary charged channel mixing. Finally, a kinematic fixed charge quadrupolar sequence develops a cooling bottleneck, while greybody contractivity and the near extremal surface gravity law exclude finite parameter attainment of extremality within that formal sequence. The sequence compares member specific reconstructed completions and is not interpreted as a physical evaporation history in one fixed nonlinear electrodynamic theory. •Hawking transport retains coupled gravitational and electromagnetic conversion.•Quadrupolar luminosity drops by over two orders of magnitude near extremality.•Bright greybody eigenchannels carry almost all thermally weighted radiation.•Mutual information reflects separable charged channel mixing, not entanglement.•Formal quadrupolar fixed charge flow cannot reach extremality in finite time.
